state: §23 lists "every channel borrowed" as a weakness (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:558).
No section states what organic discovery contributes; the research puts published-page organic at about zero (r17-h7:147).
Organic search is back-loaded to months 9 to 18 and cannot carry a launch (r17-h7:144).
Everything on the channel table, summed optimistically, reaches 350k–500k year-one visitors (r17-h7:153).
path: The channel table was built by ranking channels, not by asking what happens if none of them fires.
Today's graveyard lens supplies the control: Almanac's own 2020 Show HN scored 6 points with no comments.
Draft has served 503 people since April 2023 and drawn no Hacker News comment at all.
Both products died anyway, and the category did not notice either.
tension: Free artefacts do get attention here: human-review went from nothing to 1,241 stars in six weeks.
Attention is not payment, and nothing in that repository's numbers says anyone would pay for it.
1.4% of the 1,000 most recent Show HN posts reach 100 points, and a spike decays to zero in 96 hours.
A plan whose only channel is hand recruitment is honest, and it does not compound.

options.label: State that organic discovery contributes zero in year one, and budget nothing
options.what: One paragraph, and every other channel number becomes a claim about hand-made effort.
gains: Makes the rest of the table falsifiable rather than optimistic
Costs a paragraph
Removes the assumption that a good product gets found
costs: Reads as pessimism to anyone who has not seen the graveyard
Nothing is being built that compounds
options.money: None. It removes an implicit revenue assumption.

options.label: Keep the channel table as a ranking and add no such statement
options.what: The plan stays as it is.
gains: No argument to have
The table reads as a plan rather than a warning
costs: The optimism stays hidden inside eight rows
Nobody can tell which number depends on being found

options.label: Budget for organic on the research's own numbers, back-loaded to months 9 to 18
options.what: Fifty to two hundred thousand cumulative visitors, arriving late.
gains: Uses the research rather than a graveyard anecdote
Gives content hours a stated return to be judged against
costs: Nothing arrives inside the decision window this plan lives in
It still assumes we are found
options.money: Commits content hours against a return in year two.

options.label: Make a free artefact the discovery plan: publish a skill and see if it travels
options.what: Copy the one thing measured to travel in this category in 2026.
gains: The only observed mechanism that produced attention from nothing
Reuses the engine we already have
costs: Trains the audience that this is free
Says nothing about willingness to pay
Competes with fix-first for the same days
options.system: A published package or skill with its own release process.

recCase: The two products in the graveyard that nobody noticed had no channel written down either.
Writing the zero down is what makes every other number in the table checkable.
The alternative that has evidence, option (d), buys attention rather than payment, which is the thing already in surplus.
questions.flip: If a free artefact of ours draws a thousand stars in six weeks, discovery is real for artefacts and the statement needs a carve-out for them.
sources: research briefing 2026-09-09, graveyard lens: Draft, 503 served since April 2023

questions.q: Do we spend outreach on the git-backed CMS audience, where the review-shaped hole is already visible?
questions.lede: Pages CMS edits markdown in a repository, has no paid tier at all, and lists inline comments as "Soon".

rows.label: What it is
cells: An editor over the same files

rows.label: What the audience expects
cells: To be told why this is not

visual.caption: The right audience with the right hole, trained to expect it free.

questions.stakes: It is the most reachable adjacent audience found and the one least likely to pay for filling its own gap.
state: The channel table names no adjacent audience beyond the two agent toolchains (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:300).
Developers deploy from repositories at scale: 443,392 root CNAME files, 113,536 astro configs (docs/GAPS-2026-09-08.md:60).
Pages CMS is MIT with 3,976 stars, no paid tier, and lists inline comments as "Soon".
The gap register calls the export cut right for the wrong reason, because it used a note-taker denominator (docs/GAPS-2026-09-08.md:60).
path: Earlier rounds sized markdown audiences on Obsidian plugin downloads, which measure note-takers.
Today's research opened the git-backed CMS shelf and found the review feature unshipped.
Nothing in the plan has ever named this audience.
tension: They already keep documents in a repository, so the sidecar needs no explaining at all.
There is no paid tier anywhere in view, so they are trained to expect this free.
Outreach hours here compete directly with the two toolchain maintainers in week 2.
Obsidian's shelf shows the same shape: agent-writing plugins outweigh the only review-shaped plugin roughly forty to one.

options.label: Add it as a week-3 channel with its own integration page
options.what: A page addressed to people running a git-backed CMS.
gains: The audience needs no education about repositories

costs: Competes with the toolchain outreach for the same hours

options.label: Ignore it; the audience does not pay
options.what: The channel table stays as it is.
gains: Protects week 2 for the toolchains
No new audience to learn or to write for
costs: Gives up the only adjacency where the incumbent already names the hole
The hole stays open for whoever fills it first

gains: The fortnight needs named humans more than a channel
They already keep documents in a repository
No permission and no build
costs: No compounding effect at all
Their expectations are set by a free tool

options.label: Build the review feature Pages CMS lists as Soon, and offer it to them
options.what: Fill somebody else's roadmap gap.
gains: Directly addresses a stated need
The engine already does the hard part
costs: Builds for a project that gives everything away
Ties our roadmap to their release schedule
options.system: An integration against their storage model.
options.screens: A view inside somebody else's product.
options.money: Engineering days against an audience with no paid tier.

recCase: The fortnight needs named humans, and these are people who already keep documents in a repository.
It costs no permission, no build and no channel hours.
Whether they would pay is exactly what the ten and the twenty are for.
questions.flip: If a Pages CMS user in the pilot says they would pay, the audience is a channel and not only a recruitment pool.
